title: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 — Control of Hazardous Energy (Lockout/Tagout)
summary: Requires that all energy sources be isolated and locked/tagged before servicing. Technician must: (1) notify affected employees, (2) identify all energy sources, (3) apply lockout device, (4) release residual energy, (5) verify isolation.
key_clauses: 1910.147(c)(1): Energy control program must be established in writing.
1910.147(d)(1): Notify all affected employees before LOTO.
1910.147(d)(4): Ensure isolation of ALL energy sources — stored, electrical, hydraulic.
1910.147(d)(6): Release/restrain stored energy — bleed hydraulics, block suspended parts.
1910.147(e)(1): Verify isolation with a test device before work begins.

title: ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU — Equipment for Explosive Atmospheres
summary: All equipment and tools used in areas with explosive atmospheres (Zone 0, 1, 2) must be ATEX-certified. Non-sparking tools mandatory. No open flames. Continuous atmospheric monitoring required for hydrocarbon environments.
key_clauses: Article 2(1): 'Explosive atmosphere' means a mixture with air of flammable substances in gaseous, vapour, mist or dust form.
Annex I: Equipment for Zone 0 must be Category 1 — suitable for permanent explosive atmosphere.
Annex II: Non-electrical equipment must meet EN 13463-1 for non-sparking risk.
Requirement: Use only ATEX-certified tools. Use copper/beryllium non-sparking hand tools in hydrocarbon environments.

title: NFPA 30 — Flammable and Combustible Liquids Code
summary: Governs storage, handling, and disposal of flammable and combustible liquids. Residual hydrocarbons must be drained to approved HDPE containers, not open ground. Ventilation required. Waste classified per flashpoint.
key_clauses: NFPA 30 Section 5.3: Flammable liquids must be stored in approved containers with proper labelling.
NFPA 30 Section 5.5: Bonding and grounding required when transferring flammable liquids between metal containers.
NFPA 30 Section 17.4: Fire protection systems required in areas storing >25 gallons of Class I liquids.

title: REACH Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 — Annex XVII: Restrictions on Lead
summary: Restricts use of lead and lead compounds in manufacturing. Components with lead solder require controlled disassembly with respiratory protection (FFP3 mask minimum) and classified waste disposal per hazardous waste regs.
key_clauses: Entry 63: Lead and its compounds — restrictions on use in articles.
Disassembly rule: Lead solder must be removed under local exhaust ventilation (LEV).
PPE: FFP3 respirator, nitrile gloves mandatory when handling lead-containing components.
Waste: All lead-containing components must be segregated and disposed as hazardous waste per Directive 2008/98/EC.

title: RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU — Restriction of Hazardous Substances
summary: Restricts 10 hazardous substances in electrical/electronic equipment including lead, mercury, cadmium, and hexavalent chromium. During disassembly of EEE containing these substances, segregate restricted materials for specialist hazwaste processing.
key_clauses: Article 4(1): Electrical/electronic equipment shall not contain restricted substances.
Annex II: Maximum concentration of lead = 0.1% by weight in homogeneous material (exemptions apply).
During EoL: Subject materials must be processed at licensed WEEE facilities.

title: ISO 4126 — Safety Devices for Protection Against Excessive Pressure
summary: Defines requirements for safety relief valves and burst disc devices on pressurized systems. Before disassembly, all pressure relief paths must be confirmed open and system fully depressurized.
key_clauses: ISO 4126-1: Requirements for safety valves — ensure valve is in good condition before depressurization.
ISO 4126-4: Pilot-operated safety valves — additional caution: pilot line must be isolated first.
Verification: Use calibrated pressure gauge — visual inspection of pressure gauge alone is insufficient.
